versions.title: The runnable Canvas adaptation
versions.summary: Three local draft sets produce nine real 1080×1920 PNGs. This is the only currently verified runnable renderer in the package; it is an adaptation of a generic pipeline, not a reproduction of the historical Sayla engines.
howItWorks: Reads a local JSON config with ordered hooks, local backgrounds and a caption.
Validates paths and content, then renders one PNG per hook with a source/output manifest.
Runs without render-time networking or social/posting integration.
whatChanged: Added local-only background enforcement, captions, provenance manifests and fail-closed validation.
Rewrote payoff/caption copy as non-testimonial draft copy for the supplied examples.
caveats: All people, messages and scenarios are historical fictional/AI-generated creative; claims are unverified.
These are review previews, not publication approval, audience results or an ad-use licence.
Manual creative, claims, likeness and rights review is still required.
versions.nextStep: Inspect all nine supplied drafts, then choose the exact historical format before extending the renderer.

versions.title: The iMessage and lock-screen system
versions.summary: The missing accepted renderer has now been recovered, with its existing outputs. A personal hook leads into an authored lock-screen notification or iMessage conversation, then a Sayla payoff. These are historical fictional creatives, not real private chats.
howItWorks: Pillow composes the photo hook and phrase overlays. HTML/CSS through headless Chrome renders the authored iOS screens.
Variants a–g define narrative hooks and fictional messages; h is an authority-list treatment.
Rendering used existing photos and wallpapers. Image generation and social publishing were separate steps and are not run by this walkthrough.
whatChanged: Recovered and hash-verified 118 output images and 19 source/configuration files from the previously unavailable workstation.
54 formatted renders are shown here. Face-reference, ambiguous real-device and unformatted-background files stay out of this public projection.
The standalone local Canvas factory remains a separate engine, not a replacement for this visual system.
caveats: Historical files existing does not prove the native renderer has been rerun in this handoff.
